newsitem.title: GREECE: Construction lead Greek shares 1.63pct higher.
newsitem.headline: Construction lead Greek shares 1.63pct higher.

text.p: Market-moving macroeconomic news and good corporate reports sent Greek shares up another notch to new year highs on Friday amidst hectic trading, dealers said.
The Athens general index finished 1.63 percent or 25.12 points higher at 1,569.59, from Thursday's close of 1,544.47.
It rose steadily throughout the session, recording a new year high of 1,571.50 just before close, with construction leading the charge with gains of 2.78 percent.
Construction stocks were generally upbeat today following press reports of a new EU financial aid package for Greece in the 2000-2005 period.

"Press reports of a likely 'Santer Package' has revived the construction sector. Provided the size of the aid package is substantial, construction stocks may well build strong momentum," said Yiannis Kalogerakis, a broker with ABN-AMRO Axias Securities.
Brokers said the stock market had become more sensitive to macroeconomic news and responded positively to the latest good macroeconomic developments.
"The market has become very sensitive to macroeconomic indicators and responds favourably to recent developments," Kalogerakis said.
The Greek treasury signalled a new drop in interest rates announcing lower rates for 12M T-bills and disclosed plans for issuing long-term fixed coupon and CPI-linked bonds this month.
"Establishing a yield curve which spans a ten-year period shall make Greece a market and provide professionals with valuable tools for long-term investment planning," he said.
CPI inflation eased to 5.9 percent in April from 6.0 percent in the previous month.
Turnover grew further to 28.5 billion drachmas in volume of 8.7 million shares which was helped by active block trading.
It included the transfer of 1.2 million ex-rights shares of Hellenic Technodomiki at 2,600 drachmas, as well as OTE, 65,000 shares traded at 6,625, and Hellenic Bottling, 53,710 shares at 9,045.
Market participants welcomed the upsurge in turnover and said it was the result of fresh capital rather than typical switching between stocks.
"Growing turnover has come about from new arrivals of investors at the marketplace," Kalogerakis said.
Customer business was evenly spread among different sectors, he added.
Advancing stocks led decliners 177 to 61 with 21 stocks unchanged on 259 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted lower at 1,098-1,128. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were 75 drachmas off at 6,525 drachmas.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $79.74-$81.44. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted higher at 2,999-3,211 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $19.36-21.06. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.
--Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
